title: VX ACE Games (and other rpg maker games) are crashing with no error message.

posts.author: TheClownManGuy
posts.body: As the title says, all rpg maker games I play eventually crash with no error message. It has basically made rpg maker games nearly unplayable, I did post about this in the past but its still happening.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
and if you posted like this, then it is no wonder no one helped you - because we cannot help without details.
the simple fact that most other users have no problem with this means that the problem is somewhere on your side and not a general one, so we need to see what is wrong there.
we need at least one link (preferably more) to a specific game where you have that problem.
because there are a lot of broken projects out there that were never finished and worked for no one. And while it is unlikely it is simply possible that you never tried a finished game if you're looking for the wrong kind of free games.
second we need better descriptions of both what happens and what specs your computer have - it sounds as if the problem happens only after some longer playing, and that means it may be memory leaks in the engine, especially if your computer is low on RAM.
For example pre-1.4.x RMMV had massive memory leaks in its engine. Those were fixed with later versions, but if you only played games that were never updated to 1.5 or 1,6...

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
TheClownManGuy said:
They all crash without showing an error message eventually and at random times.
Click to expand...
an internal, engine based crash should always cause an error message, especially on newer makers (MV and MZ).
If there is no error message, then it is very likely that this is not a crash but an external shutdown override.
How long does it take until the problem? five minutes, one hour, multiple hours of playing?
The main causes for an external override are a false positive from a protection program like a firewall or antivirus (especially for MV and MZ that are often mistaken for infected websites due to being HTML-based), or a damaged driver (audio or video) getting the wrong data.
